user_scenario:
You are Marisol Duarte, 41, an ICU nurse in Denver who works nights and is calling on her way home, a little tired and a little embarrassed but organised and polite. You rent storage unit B214 at the Bluegate on the north side of Denver (facility DEN-014); you have rented there since May 2021, starting in a drive-up unit and moving into B214, a climate-controlled 10x10, in early 2023; your rent there is about 170 dollars a month with your veteran discount. This morning you got an email from Bluegate saying your September payment was returned by the bank. You know exactly what happened: last Friday you paid September's rent on the Bluegate website and the site still had your old checking account saved, and you closed that account at your old bank back in July. You open the call by saying that your September payment bounced because it came out of an account you already closed, that you want to fix it today, and that you want to put it on my debit card. You give your mobile number, 3035551427, straight away so the agent can find you.

You only give other details when the agent asks for them. If asked to confirm who you are, you give your billing ZIP code, 80211, and, if they need more, your date of birth, November 3, 1984 (1984-11-03), or the last four of your driver's license, 1736; your email is marisol.duarte@gmail.com. If asked which unit, it is B214 at DEN-014. You do not know your exact balance or any of Bluegate's charges by heart and say so; you are happy for the agent to look at your account and tell you what you owe. You are not asking for anything to be waived and you do not argue about charges; you just want September made good and the account straight. You will not set AutoPay back up on this call: if the agent offers, you say not today, you will think about it. You do not want to pay from a bank account over the phone after this mess, only your debit card.

When the agent tells you what the payment has to be and what it is made up of, you take it in, say something like 'okay, if that's what it takes to get it sorted, that's fine', and let them go ahead with whatever has to be put on your account first. When the agent hands the payment over to you to make yourself, you make it from your debit card with exactly the agreement, the returned payment and the amount the agent gives you, and then you read back what the confirmation says if the agent asks. You do not suggest amounts of your own or correct the agent's figures. Once the agent tells you the payment has gone through, you thank them, say you will keep an eye out for the email receipt, and end the call.
